key_insight: GDPO decouples reward-group normalization from policy updates so each reward signal is scaled and optimized independently, yielding more stable and balanced multi-reward policy learning than prior Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) approaches.
problem_solved: Existing multi-reward RL pipelines (e.g., GRPO) struggle when rewards differ in scale or conflict, causing instability, poor trade-offs among objectives, and dominance by a subset of rewards.
method: Introduce group reward-decoupled normalization: rescale or normalize each reward group independently before computing policy updates to prevent cross-reward interference.
Integrate the decoupled normalization into a policy optimization loop (GDPO) so per-group baselines and gradients are handled separately while still updating a single policy.
Validate with theoretical analysis and experiments showing improved convergence, fairness across objectives, and reduced variance compared to GRPO baselines.
impact: GDPO enables more reliable multi-objective fine-tuning of language models and other RL agents, improving alignment with diverse user preferences and reducing training instability—useful for RLHF and any multi-reward optimization tasks.
visual_elements: Before/After schematic: GRPO vs GDPO showing how combined vs decoupled normalization affects gradient flow

Radar or bar chart showing improved balanced performance across several reward axes (trade-off visualization)
paper_title: GDPO: Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization for Multi-reward RL Optimization
paper_authors: Shih-Yang Liu, Xin Dong, Ximing Lu, Shizhe Diao, Peter Belcak
